newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire imposes night curfew on Kinshasa.
newsitem.headline: Zaire imposes night curfew on Kinshasa.

text.p: The government of Zaire on Tuesday declared a curfew in the capital Kinshasa from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. and told people to stay off the streets.
"The government has decreed a curfew on all of the city of Kinshasa from the hours of 2000 to 0600 which will take effect today," Information Minister Kin-Kiey Mulumba told reporters.

Troops would have orders to open fire on any looters after issuing three warnings in accordance with the law, Mulumba said. The decision was taken at a national security meeting of the cabinet including the defence and interior ministers.
It was the first time a curfew had been imposed on Kinshasa since the rebels who now control three quarters of the country took up arms against President Mobutu Sese Seko's government last October.
Mulumba said street patrols by army and police would be reinforced, checkpoints established and strategic locations placed under high surveillance.
Kinshasa, a city of five million people, was calm on Tuesday, but in the words of one radio commentator "the people have lost their smiles."
